   (let [served (serve session budget)
         session (:session served)
         engine (:engine session)
         [engine' text]
         (if (:progress? served)
           (repl/recheck-pending engine)
           (repl/recheck-on-tick engine
                                 (completion/completion-events session
                                                               events)))]
     [(assoc session :engine engine') text])))


(defn recheck-pending
  "One re-check of the parked run without a tick's events — the step an
  unattended host drives at its own cadence.  Answers `[session' text]`,
  `text` nil when nothing is pending."
  [session]
  (let [[engine text] (repl/recheck-pending (:engine session))]
    [(assoc session :engine engine) text]))


(defn settle-publication
  "`session` after every publication result its composition has already
  appended is consumed.  A composition that services its own medium
  locally leaves nothing to consume and this is a no-op; one with
  transport of its own calls it once it has delivered, before it reports
  the round settled (docs/design/yin.repl.dht-composition.md section 3)."
  [session]
  (update session :engine repl/settle-publication))
(ns yin.shell.linker
  "Linker progression, composition-side
   (docs/design/yin.repl.dht-composition.md section 7).

   The engine drives the links it can serve itself — a local `dao.jing`
   content store, a remote content client, a bare name environment —
   through `yin.vm.linker.interpreter/round-local`, which takes no node.
   A signed-name source instead reads its content from a node its
   composition is handed each round, so this namespace owns that round:
   it is the only place `round`'s `[linker node]` interface survives, and
   no node crosses inward to the engine from here.

   The composition value is plain data, `{:linker … :link-source … :node
   …}`.  `:linker` is the interpreter value whose generic protocol state —
   link pair, request cursor, admission — the engine carries too, and
   `:node` is the transport's alone.  `serve-links` answers its successor;
   `install` writes back only the generic half, so an engine reading the
   result sees correlated decisions and generic pending-work identities
   and never names a node."
  (:require [yin.vm.linker.interpreter :as link]))


(defn from-engine
  "The composition value an `engine` state and its transport `node`
   compose: the linker and the source it serves read off the engine, the
   node supplied.  A composition with no transport answers `node` nil, and
   the round then serves only what the interpreter serves itself."
  [engine node]
  {:linker (:linker engine)
   :link-source (:link-source engine)
   :node node})


(defn serve-links
  "One composition round of linker progression, the section 7
   `serve-links`: consume the link request media the engine's VMs appended
   to, and answer `{:composition c' :pending p :answered n :progress?
   bool}`.

   `c'` carries the successor linker and the successor node, `p` the
   generic pending-work identities the round could not settle — each
   naming the manifest it waits on under `:manifest`, or the principals it
   waits on under `:principals`, or the admission question under
   `:admission` — and `:progress?` says the round moved something, the
   fact a composition pairs with a pending run's re-check.  The engine is
   not an argument and is not returned: only `install` crosses back."
  ([composition] (serve-links composition link/serve-budget))
  ([{:keys [linker link-source node] :as composition} budget]
   (let [served (link/round (cond-> linker
                              link-source (assoc :source link-source))
                            node
                            budget)]
     {:composition (assoc composition
                          :linker (:linker served)
                          :node (:dht served))
      :pending (:pending served)
      :answered (:answered served)
      :progress? (:progress? served)})))


(defn install
  "`engine` with the composition's served linker successor installed, and
   with nothing else: the generic protocol state crosses back, the node
   stays the composition's."
  [engine composition]
  (assoc engine :linker (:linker composition)))


(defn retire
  "The composition side of an abandoned run: retire the run's requests
   still unread on the link pair, so a later require on the same pair is
   served and a response already in flight is skipped as late.  `run` is
   the generic descriptor the engine mints
   (`yin.vm.linker.interpreter/run-descriptor`); this namespace adds no
   identity of its own."
  [composition run]
  (update composition :linker link/retire run))
(ns yin.shell.completion
  "Event filtering, composition-side
   (docs/design/yin.repl.dht-composition.md section 7).

   A transport step answers events in its own vocabulary.  The engine may
   see none of it: `completion-events` translates the two outcomes a parked
   `(require ...)` can wait on into correlated generic completions, keyed
   by the identity the engine already holds for the parked work — the
   manifest address of a load, the principal id of a followed head.  An
   event that names neither is dropped here rather than forwarded, so the
   engine re-checks only matching parked work, ignores everything else,
   and resumes each completion once.

   The two generic shapes the engine's `yin.repl/recheck-on-tick` reads
   are `{:op :dependency :manifest address :status :loaded|:load-failed}`
   and `{:op :principal :principal id :status :installed}`.  Both are
   plain data and neither names a backend; this namespace is the only
   place on either side of the seam that knows which keyword a load or a
   head install arrived under.")


(def load-outcomes
  "The transport load outcomes that end a wait: a closure that arrived and
   one that failed are both completions, and a parked require re-checks on
   either — the refusal it then reads is the link's, not the event's."
  #{:loaded :load-failed})


(defn dependency-event
  "The generic completion for one transport load outcome `event`, or nil
   for an event that is not a load ending."
  [event]
  (let [status (:dao.space.dht/event event)]
    (when (contains? load-outcomes status)
      {:op :dependency
       :manifest (:manifest event)
       :status status})))


(defn principal-event
  "The generic completion for one follower outcome `event`, or nil for an
   event that is not a head installed.  A head that moved or failed is not
   a completion: nothing parked is waiting to be told about it, and a name
   the move displaced is re-resolved on the round that re-checks."
  [event]
  (when (= :installed (:yin.head/event event))
    {:op :principal
     :principal (:principal event)
     :status :installed}))


(defn completion-events
  "`events` — the transport and follower events one composition step
  produced — as the vector of generic completions the engine may see, in
  the order they arrived.  `composition` is the composition value, so a
  translation that must consult what the composition follows or has
  loaded can; the two translations here are keyed by the event alone.

  An event that is neither a load ending nor a head install contributes
  nothing, so a step's banners, acknowledgements and refusals never cross
  inward."
  ([events] (completion-events nil events))
  ([_composition events]
   (into []
         (keep (fn [event]
                 (or (dependency-event event)
                     (principal-event event))))
         events)))
(ns yin.shell.registry
  "The neutral projection of a VM module registry to the linked names it
   holds (docs/design/yin.repl.dht-composition.md section 6).

   A linked module's entry carries its manifest's address and a host
   module's carries none, so `{name manifest-address}` of a registry is
   pure data over `yin.vm.module` and belongs to no storage backend.  It
   lives here, apart from any composition, because the two sides that
   need it — a composition's signed-name service and the composition
   module that moves a followed head — must not reach it through each
   other."
  (:require [yin.vm.module :as module]))


(defn linked-registry
  "`{name manifest-address}` of the modules a VM module `registry` holds
   linked through the linker: a linked entry carries its manifest's
   address, a host module none."
  [registry]
  (into {}
        (keep (fn [[n e]] (when (some? (:address e)) [n (:address e)])))
        (module/module-entries registry)))


(defn host-module-names
  "The set of names of `registry`'s host modules: the entries that carry
   no manifest address, because a host module is a registration and not a
   linked image."
  [registry]
  (set (keep (fn [[n e]] (when (nil? (:address e)) n))
             (module/module-entries registry))))


(defn session-modules
  "`[linked hosts]` of the requesting VM's module `registry`: the modules
   it linked through the linker, and the names of its host modules.  The
   pair a signed-name publication declares beside the code it publishes."
  [registry]
  [(linked-registry registry) (host-module-names registry)])

(ns yin.vm.linker.interpreter
  "The REPL's linker-side composition (yin.vm.linker.md sections 6.1 and 9,
   M5): the interpreter box of the four-stream topology.

   The shell composes the link pair per VM (`yin.repl/make-session`) and
   the content pair per content source; this namespace owns the second
   and answers what the first receives.  One serve round reads every link
   request the interpreter has not yet seen, resolves each by name
   through the composition's name environment -- the snapshot the host
   supplies, an authority fold (`yin.vm.linker.authority/name-environment`)
   reduced to `name -> manifest address` -- and links the manifest's
   image over the content pair, appending the response the requesting
   task correlates on (section 7.2, steps 5 to 6).

   Step 5b is deferred: the obligations travel on the response and the
   receiving task's engine discharges them against its live state
   (section 7.2, step 7), so the interpreter passes
   `:defer-discharge` to `link-manifest` and discharges nothing here.

   Liveness is the composition's (section 6.3, D6): an attempt serves the
   content pair for at most `attempt-budget` drive rounds and then
   reports the link `:pending` -- nothing is appended, the request is
   re-read and re-attempted on a later round, and `abandon` is the
   shell's.  No clock, no atom, no global: every input is an argument or
   a composition value, and every outcome is plain data.

   A DHT link source (docs/design/yin.vm.linker.dht.md 4.1) holds no
   handle: each serve round receives the shell's `dao.space.dht` node
   and answers the node after it.  A resolved name whose closure is not
   loaded starts its load (`yin.vm.linker.dht/load-module`) and reports
   the link `:pending`, naming the manifest it waits on; the node's own
   step fetches.  A failed load is refused in its section 9 shape and
   forgotten; a loaded one has its dependency bindings checked, then
   links over a local runtime on the node's store, asking no peer."
  (:require [clojure.string :as str]
            [dao.jing.content :as content]
            [dao.space.dht :as dht]
            [dao.stream :as stream]
            [dao.stream.ringbuffer :as ring]
            [yin.vm.linker :as linker]
            [yin.vm.linker.admission :as admission]
            [yin.vm.linker.dht :as linker.dht]
            [yin.vm.linker.sign :as sign]))


(def pair-capacity
  "Declared capacity of each link-pair medium, in elements.  The shell
   appends one request per require, and a response medium a receiver
   never drains answers `gap` (an evicted request is never re-read), so
   the bound is generous and the eviction it guards against is a host
   assembly defect, not an operating condition."
  1024)


(def content-capacity
  "Declared capacity of each content-pair medium, in elements.  One
   attempt's traffic is a handful of requests; the media persist across
   attempts and every attempt mints its cursors at their newest end, so
   an old element is never read again."
  1024)


(def attempt-budget
  "Drive rounds one link attempt may spend before it reports `:pending`.
   A local pair answers within a few rounds per content request, so the
   budget is reached only by a content source that never answers."
  64)


(def serve-steps
  "Server advances one drive round performs at most.  Each answers at
   least one waiting content request, so a local pair drains in a bound
   number of rounds."
  32)


(def serve-budget
  "Link requests one serve round answers, in request order.  It exceeds
   what one evaluation's requires can enqueue, so a round that spends it
   is answering a queue the shell did not write."
  64)


(def formats
  "The six format records a serving composition holds (sections 5 and
   8.1): the four execution formats a requesting kernel names, and the
   two the manifest flow fetches internally."
  (into {}
        (map (fn [r] [(:format r) r]))
        [linker/ast-format linker/semantic-format
         linker/stack-format
         linker/register-format linker/manifest-format
         linker/record-format]))


(defn- medium
  [capacity]
  (:dao.stream/handle
    (ring/create! {:dao.stream/type ring/transport-type
                   ring/capacity-key capacity})))


(defn- newest
  [handle]
  (:dao.stream/cursor (stream/cursor handle stream/anchor-newest)))


(defn make-pair
  "The link pair of one session (section 6.1): the request and response
   media, `capacity` elements each (`pair-capacity` by default), and the
   interpreter's own request cursor, minted before any request exists."
  ([] (make-pair pair-capacity))
  ([capacity]
   (let [requests (medium capacity)
         responses (medium capacity)]
     {:requests requests
      :responses responses
      :cursor (:dao.stream/cursor
                (stream/cursor requests stream/anchor-oldest))})))


(defn composition
  "The content side of the shell's link composition, from the host's
   creation options.  `content-store` is a `dao.jing` byte-store handle
   served in process over its own ring-buffer content pair (the
   single-process and durable-local rows of section 6.1);
   `content-client` is the linker's content-pair client map
   `{:requests w :answers r :cursor c}` on a connection whose far end
   serves content (the remote-content row), and the drive then only
   steps the linker, the server running elsewhere (section 6.4).  A
   content source is optional: with none, every link stays `:pending`
   and says so.  Supplying both is a composition defect.  `dht?` is the
   DHT link source (yin.vm.linker.dht.md 4.1): it reads content from the
   node each serve round is handed, holds nothing here, and is refused
   together with either content source.

   `principals` are the public keys (64 lowercase hex) whose signed name
   assertions the reader honors (yin.vm.linker.dht.md 7.1), and `key`
   the node's own publisher key, whose principal is declared too (6.5):
   a node resolves the names it published.  Only the public half is
   kept here.  `follow` are the principal ids (`ed25519:<hex>`) whose
   published heads the DHT source follows (yin.vm.linker.dht.head.md
   5.6): a name that is `:absent` while one of them has no installed head
   is pending on it, not refused.

   `derivation` is the composition's derivation policy (section 8.1) for
   the manifest links it serves from a content source: `:verifying`, the
   default, or `:trusted`, which only a composition that is its own
   publisher asks for. The response names the trust it applied.

   `admission`, optional, is the policy of the in-process admission
   interpreter (yin.vm.linker.dht.md 7.5,
   `yin.vm.linker.admission/policy`):
   `{:trusted #{principal} :verify f :decision d :decision-medium m}`,
   the key's own principal joining it as `:own`.  Without it no
   interpreter runs in process: the questions a DHT source asks are
   answered elsewhere or not at all. `:holder` is the context subject,
   a principal id or a token understood by verify; it defaults to the
   own key's principal.

(ns yin.shell.query
  "Query and name services, composition-side
   (docs/design/yin.repl.dht-composition.md sections 6 and 7).

   The three host modules a signed-name composition serves through —
   `dao.space.dht`, `yin.link` and `yin.head` — are registered here and
   answered here, over the node the composition owns.  The engine's own
   query surface (`yin.repl.query`) keeps the local `dao.space.query`
   bridge and its bounded request/response semantics, reads no node, and
   leaves a request under one of these operations unread on the shared
   pair (`yin.repl.query/foreign-request?`) for this namespace to answer.

   `registrations` is what a composition hands `yin.repl.query/register`,
   the generic module-registration mechanism; `serve-services` is the
   section 7 adapter, and it answers a local query too, so a composition
   that holds the pair's cursor never leaves a request behind it.

   This namespace holds no rule of the head trace, no fold, no
   verification and no file write: each answer checks its arguments, makes
   one call into the plain API of the implementation it composes, and
   responds.  A `yin.link/publish` additionally commits the envelopes it
   signed through the session's indexer, which is the generic commit the
   engine owns."
  (:require [dao.jing :as jing]
            [dao.space.dht :as dht]
            [dao.stream :as stream]
            [dao.stream.apply :as apply2]
            [yin.repl :as repl]
            [yin.repl.index :as repl.index]
            [yin.repl.query :as query]
            [yin.shell.registry :as shell.registry]
            [yin.vm :as vm]
            [yin.vm.linker.dht :as linker.dht]
            [yin.vm.linker.head :as head]
            [yin.vm.linker.interpreter :as link]
            [yin.vm.module :as module]
            ;; the follower accessor lives in the composition module that
            ;; section 6 relocates to yin.shell.dht; this require moves
            ;; with it
            [yin.repl.dht :as repl.dht]))


(def dht-module-name
  "The module `(require 'dao.space.dht)` activates: the plain Clojure DHT
   path (`dao.space.dht`) as host functions over the composition's node."
  'dao.space.dht)


(def dht-ops
  "The `dao.stream.apply` operations the `dao.space.dht` module requests:
   `load-index`, `load-status` and `q`, each answered by the
   `dao.space.dht` function of that name, `retry` and `cancel`, answered
   by `retry!` and `cancel!`, and `load-module` and `module-status`,
   answered by the `yin.vm.linker.dht` function of that name
   (yin.vm.linker.dht.md 10)."
  {'load-index ::dht-load-index
   'load-status ::dht-load-status
   'q ::dht-q
   'retry ::dht-retry
   'cancel ::dht-cancel
   'load-module ::dht-load-module
   'module-status ::dht-module-status})


(def dht-arities
  "The primitive profile arity each `dao.space.dht` export is registered
   under."
  {'load-index [1] 'load-status [1] 'q [2 :variadic] 'retry [1] 'cancel [1]
   'load-module [1] 'module-status [1]})


(def link-module-name
  "The module `(require 'yin.link)` activates: publishing a module from
   the session's indexed code and reading the reader's name environment
   (yin.vm.linker.dht.md 10), over the composition's node."
  'yin.link)


(def link-ops
  "The `dao.stream.apply` operations the `yin.link` module requests:
   `publish`, answered by `yin.vm.linker.dht/publish-name!`, and `names`,
   answered by `yin.vm.linker.dht/names`."
  {'publish ::link-publish
   'names ::link-names})


(def head-module-name
  "The module `(require 'yin.head)` activates: the follower's status and
   the moved names (yin.vm.linker.dht.head.md 5.6, 5.7), each one call
   into `yin.vm.linker.head`."
  'yin.head)


(def head-ops
  "The `dao.stream.apply` operations the `yin.head` module requests:
   `heads`, answered by `yin.vm.linker.head/heads` of the composition's
   follower, and `moved`, by `yin.vm.linker.head/moved`."
  {'heads ::head-heads
   'moved ::head-moved})


;; =============================================================================
;; The module registrations (yin.repl.query/register's generic mechanism)
;; =============================================================================

(defn- effect-export
  "An export of a module this namespace serves: a data constructor whose
   effect parks the caller on the session's query call pair, under the
   operation `op` names.  The effect key is the engine's
   (`yin.repl.query/call-effect`), so the one handler the session
   registers parks these calls beside its own `q`."
  [op]
  (fn [& args]
    (module/make-effect query/call-effect {:op op, :args (vec args)})))


(defn- dht-export
  "A `dao.space.dht` export, parking under the operation `dht-ops` names
   for `sym`."
  [sym]
  (effect-export (get dht-ops sym)))


(defn activate-dht
  "`registry` with the `dao.space.dht` host module installed."
  [registry]
  (module/register-host-module
    registry dht-module-name
    (into {} (map (fn [sym] [sym (dht-export sym)])) (keys dht-ops))
    (into {} (map (fn [[sym arity]]
                    [sym (vm/primitive-profile
                           sym :effectful arity #{query/call-effect} :none)]))
          dht-arities)))


(defn activate-link
  "`registry` with the `yin.link` host module installed."
  [registry]
  (module/register-host-module
    registry link-module-name
    (into {} (map (fn [[sym op]] [sym (effect-export op)])) link-ops)
    {'publish (vm/primitive-profile 'publish :effectful [2]
                                    #{query/call-effect} :none)
     'names (vm/primitive-profile 'names :effectful [0]
                                  #{query/call-effect} :none)}))


(defn activate-head
  "`registry` with the `yin.head` host module installed."
  [registry]
  (module/register-host-module
    registry head-module-name
    (into {} (map (fn [[sym op]] [sym (effect-export op)])) head-ops)
    {'heads (vm/primitive-profile 'heads :effectful [0]
                                  #{query/call-effect} :none)
     'moved (vm/primitive-profile 'moved :effectful [0]
                                  #{query/call-effect} :none)}))


(def registrations
  "The host module registrations a signed-name composition supplies to
   `yin.repl.query/register`.  A composition that serves none of them
   supplies none, and its sessions never see these names."
  {dht-module-name activate-dht
   link-module-name activate-link
   head-module-name activate-head})


;; =============================================================================
;; Answering one call
;; =============================================================================

(defn- host-status
  "A load status as the host answers it: the status without its loaded
   value, which an index load counts under `:datoms` instead."
  [status]
  (when status
    (cond-> (dissoc status :value)
      (and (= :loaded (:status status)) (= dht/index-kind (:kind status)))
      (assoc :datoms (count (:value status))))))


(defn- refusable-call
  "`[node' answer]` of the plain function `f` on `node` and `manifest`:
   `(ok node')` answers; a `:dao.space.dht/refused` of any code is
   answered under its own code, the node unchanged."
  [node manifest f ok]
  (try (let [node (f node manifest)] [node {:ok (ok node)}])
       (catch #?(:cljd Object :clj Exception :cljs :default) e
         (if-let [code (:dao.space.dht/refused (ex-data e))]
           [node (query/refusal code (ex-message e) nil)]
           (throw e)))))


(defn- publication-call
  "`[node' answer]` of `retry!` or `cancel!` on `manifest`: `ok` answers
   `ok`; the plain function's refusal is answered under its own code."
  [node manifest f ok]
  (refusable-call node manifest f (constantly ok)))


(defn- no-node
  "The refusal a session with no transport answers every one of these
   calls with."
  [module-name hint]
  (query/unavailable (str "the shell has no " module-name " node; start it "
                          "with " hint)))


(defn- dht-answer
  "The response to one `dao.space.dht` call, answered from `node` — the
   composition's node — by the `dao.space.dht` function the operation
   names, and the node after it: `load-index` starts a load and answers
   its status at once, never waiting, or the plain function's refusal
   under its own code (`load-module` likewise); `load-status` answers the
   load's status map; `q` answers `dao.space.dht/q` under `limits`, refused
   until the index is loaded; `retry` and `cancel` answer `:retrying` and
   `:cancelled`, or the plain function's refusal; `load-module` starts a
   closure load and answers its status, and `module-status` answers it
   without the loaded closure.  Answers `[node response]`."
  [node limits request]
  (let [id (apply2/request-id request)
        [manifest & more] (apply2/request-args request)
        [node answer]
        (cond
          (nil? node)
          [node (no-node "DHT" "--index-store dht:<dir> and --dht-peer")]

          (nil? (query/encoded-size (apply2/request-args request)))
          [node (query/invalid "dao.space.dht takes portable Yin data only")]

          (not (jing/segment-address? manifest))
          [node (query/invalid
                  (str "dao.space.dht expects a manifest address, got "
                       (pr-str manifest)))]

          :else
          (case (apply2/request-op request)
            ::dht-load-index
            (refusable-call node manifest dht/load-index
                            #(:status (dht/load-status % manifest)))

            ::dht-load-status
            [node {:ok (host-status (dht/load-status node manifest))}]

            ::dht-load-module
            (refusable-call node manifest linker.dht/load-module
                            #(:status (linker.dht/module-status % manifest)))

            ::dht-module-status
            [node {:ok (host-status (linker.dht/module-status node manifest))}]

            ::dht-retry
            (publication-call node manifest dht/retry! :retrying)

            ::dht-cancel
            (publication-call node manifest dht/cancel! :cancelled)

            ::dht-q
            (let [status (dht/load-status node manifest)
                  [q & inputs] more]
              [node (if (= :loaded (:status status))
                      (query/bounded
                        #(apply dht/q node manifest q inputs) limits)
                      (query/refusal

                             (if status (name (:status status)) "never asked")
                             "); (dao.space.dht/load-index " manifest
                             ") loads it")
                        nil))])))]

(defn- link-answer
  "The response to one `yin.link` call, from `node` — the composition's
   node — and `indexer`, the session's code indexer, under the session
   context `ctx` (`:authority`, `:key`, `:primitives`, `:modules`,
   `:round`): `names` answers `yin.vm.linker.dht/names`; `publish` answers
   `yin.vm.linker.dht/publish-name!` over the published index, whose name
   envelopes the indexer then commits and publishes as one transaction,
   the composition's durable HEAD write announcing the round's
   publication.  A refusal is answered under its own reason.  Answers
   `[node indexer response]`."
  [node indexer ctx request]
  (let [id (apply2/request-id request)
        args (apply2/request-args request)
        [indexer answer]
        (cond
          (nil? node)
          [indexer (no-node "DHT" "--index-store dht:<dir>")]

          (nil? (query/encoded-size args))
          [indexer (query/invalid "yin.link takes portable Yin data only")]

          (= ::link-names (apply2/request-op request))
          [indexer {:ok (linker.dht/names node (:authority ctx))}]

          :else
          (let [[name exports] args
                db (when (and (symbol? name) (sequential? exports)
                              (every? symbol? exports))
                     (query/snapshot indexer))]
            (cond
              (nil? db)
              [indexer (query/invalid
                         (str "yin.link/publish expects a module name and a "
                              "vector of export names, got " (pr-str args)))]

              (query/refused? db) [indexer db]

              :else
              (let [[linked hosts] (shell.registry/session-modules
                                     (:modules ctx))
                    res (linker.dht/publish-name!
                          node db {:name name
                                   :exports (vec exports)
                                   :key (:key ctx)
                                   :primitives (:primitives ctx)
                                   :modules linked
                                   :host-modules hosts})
                    indexer' (if (seq (:envelopes res))
                               (repl.index/commit-names
                                 indexer (:envelopes res) (:round ctx))
                               indexer)]
                (cond
                  (= :refused (:status res))
                  [indexer (query/refusal
                             (:reason res)
                             (str "yin.link/publish refused: "
                                  (pr-str (dissoc res :status :reason)))
                             nil)]

                  (not= (:failure indexer) (:failure indexer'))
                  [indexer' (query/unavailable
                              "the name assertion was not indexed")]

                  :else
                  [indexer'
                   {:ok {:module name
                         :address (:address res)
                         :links (into {}
                                      (map (fn [[f o]]
                                             [f (if (= :ok (:status o))
                                                  :ok
                                                  (:reason o))]))
                                      (:links res))}}])))))]
    [node indexer (query/response id answer)]))


(defn- head-answer
  "The response to one `yin.head` call, from `node`, the composition's
   node, under the session context `ctx`: `heads` answers
   `yin.vm.linker.head/heads` of the node's follower (`{}` when it follows
   nothing), `moved` answers `yin.vm.linker.head/moved` of the node's
   names against the requesting VM's linked modules.  It holds no rule:
   each is one call."
  [node ctx request]
  (let [id (apply2/request-id request)
        answer (cond
                 (nil? node)
                 (no-node "DHT" "--index-store dht:<dir>")

                 (= ::head-heads (apply2/request-op request))
                 {:ok (if-some [f (repl.dht/follower node)] (head/heads f) {})}

                 :else
                 {:ok (head/moved
                        (linker.dht/names node (:authority ctx))
                        (first (shell.registry/session-modules
                                 (:modules ctx))))})]
    (query/response id answer)))


;; =============================================================================
;; The adapter (docs/design/yin.repl.dht-composition.md section 7)
;; =============================================================================

(def default-budget
  "Requests one `serve-services` round answers.  It matches the engine's
   own query serve budget, so a composition holding the pair's cursor
   drains a round exactly as far as the engine would."
  64)


(defn default-limits
  "The row and encoded-byte bounds of a composition that declares none of
   its own: the engine's, so a call answered composition-side is bounded
   exactly as one answered engine-side."
  []
  {:row-limit repl/query-row-limit
   :byte-limit repl/query-byte-limit})


(defn- op-in?
  [ops request]
  (contains? (set (vals ops)) (apply2/request-op request)))


(defn- serve-round
  "One round over the session's query call pair, answering the three
   modules this namespace serves and delegating a local
   `dao.space.query` call to the engine's own interpreter
   (`yin.repl.query/answer`), so a composition that holds the cursor never
   leaves a request behind it.  Answers `{:pair :node :indexer :progress?
   :answered}`."
  [{:keys [pair indexer ast-indexer node limits budget link]}]
  (loop [pair pair
         node node
         indexer indexer
         remaining budget
         progress? false
         answered 0]
    (let [done (fn [node indexer progress? answered]
                 {:pair pair, :node node, :indexer indexer,
                  :progress? progress?, :answered answered})
          r (when (pos? remaining)
              (stream/next (:call-in pair) (:cursor pair)))]
      (if-not (= :dao.stream/ok (:dao.stream/outcome r))
        (done node indexer progress? answered)
        (let [request (:dao.stream/value r)
              [node' indexer' response]
              (cond
                (not (apply2/request? request)) [node indexer nil]
                (op-in? dht-ops request)
                (let [[n response] (dht-answer node limits request)]
                  [n indexer response])
                (op-in? link-ops request) (link-answer node indexer link request)
                (op-in? head-ops request) [node indexer (head-answer node link request)]
                :else [node indexer
                       (query/answer indexer ast-indexer limits request)])
              landed? (or (nil? response)
                          (= :dao.stream/ok
                             (:dao.stream/outcome
                               (apply2/put-response! (:call-out pair)
                                                     response))))]
          (if landed?
            (recur (assoc pair :cursor (:dao.stream/cursor r))
                   node'
                   indexer'
                   (dec remaining)
                   true
                   (cond-> answered response inc))
            (done node indexer progress? answered)))))))


(defn service-context
  "The context a signed service call is answered under: the explicit
   request data the engine supplies (`yin.repl/service-context` — the
   requesting VM's primitives, its module registry and the round) with the
   two halves only a composition may hold added, the reader's authority
   derived from the link source and the publisher's key.  The engine
   carries neither."
  [engine publisher-key]
  (merge (repl/service-context engine (:vm engine))
         {:authority (link/authority (:link-source engine))
          :key publisher-key}))


(defn serve-services
  "One composition round of query and name serving, the section 7
   `serve-services`: interpret the calls the session's VMs appended to the
   shared query pair, and answer `{:composition c' :progress? bool
   :answered n}`.

   `composition` is `{:engine <the engine state> :node <the transport's
   node or nil> :key <the publisher's key or nil> :limits {:row-limit n
   :byte-limit n}}`.  `c'` carries the successor node and the successor
   engine, whose query cursor and indexer this round moved; nothing else
   of the engine is touched, and no node crosses inward."
  ([composition] (serve-services composition default-budget))
  ([{:keys [engine node limits] :as composition} budget]
   (let [served (serve-round {:pair (:query-pair engine)
                              :indexer (:indexer engine)
                              :ast-indexer (:ast-indexer engine)
                              :node node
                              :limits (or limits (default-limits))
                              :budget budget
                              :link (service-context engine
                                                     (:key composition))})]
     {:composition (-> composition
                       (assoc :node (:node served))
                       (update :engine assoc
                               :query-pair (:pair served)
                               :indexer (:indexer served)))
      :progress? (:progress? served)
      :answered (:answered served)})))

(defn- make-expander
  "The expander consumer for one session: a fresh incarnation token, the
   `program-in` identity as its source medium, the standard store, and the
   `program-out` writer.  No log writer: `(compile ...)` renders events."
  [program-identity program-out]
  (macro/make-expander
    (macro/make-ctx {:token (str (random-uuid))
                     :source-medium program-identity
                     :store (standard-store)})
    program-out))


(defn- make-session
  "Build the evaluator, its media, their attachments and observers, the
   expander, and the loader the evaluator observer feeds the VM, together.
   Reset and VM selection call this, so the whole composition is rebuilt as
   one and each attachment capability is bound exactly once per medium
   lifetime.

   Both evaluators sit behind the same two stages (yin.vm.macro.md §10.1):
   the expander observes `program-in` — `:program-stream`, watched by
   `:observer` — and appends each expanded tree packet to `program-out` —
   `:row-stream`, watched independently by the evaluator's `:row-observer`,
   which loads each packet and runs it.  The code indexer's observer
   (`yin.repl.index`) is a peer attached to `program-out` beside it; the
   round advances each, and neither calls the other.  It records
   `shell-token` as provenance and publishes into `index-store`.  The AST
   indexer (`yin.repl.ast-index`), holding the session's `$ast` and `$occ`
   relations, is a third such peer.

   The session owns one linker value. Its source configuration outlives
   a session rebuild.

   The query call pair is the session's too (`yin.repl.query/make-pair`):
   the VM's half is its FFI pair, the interpreter's half with its request
   cursor sits under `:query-pair`, and the interpreter answers from the
   session's `:indexer`, and `:ast-indexer` for `$ast` and `$occ`, as they
   stand when it serves.

   A durable store's HEAD write is the composition's, reached over the
   publication medium pair (`yin.repl.publication`): every session the
   store outlives publishes through the same one.

   `host-modules` is the composition's module registrations, installed
   into every session's registry so a rebuild never drops them
   (`make-vm`)."
  [vm-type output-stream extra-primitives shell-token index-store source
   publication host-modules]
  (let [linker (link/make source)
        pair (:pair linker)
        query-pair (query/make-pair query-pair-capacity)
        vm (make-vm vm-type output-stream extra-primitives pair query-pair
                    host-modules)
        program-in (make-attachment ingress-capacity)
        program-out (make-attachment ingress-capacity)]
    {:vm vm
     :load-program (get program-loaders vm-type)
     :program-stream (:stream program-in)
     :program-identity (:identity program-in)
     :observer (:observer program-in)
     :expander (make-expander (:identity program-in) (:stream program-out))
     :row-stream (:stream program-out)
     :row-observer (:observer program-out)
     :indexer (index/make-indexer {:observer ((:attach program-out))
                                   :session-token shell-token
                                   :content-store index-store
                                   :publish-opts (or (:publication-policy publication)
                                                     (:publish-opts index-store))
                                   :publication-media (:media publication)})
     :ast-indexer (ast-index/make-indexer {:observer ((:attach program-out))})
     :linker linker
     :query-pair (dissoc query-pair :out-cursor)}))


(defn- checked-link-policy
  "Validate the `:link-policy` creation option, failing closed at
   assembly (yin.repl.link-policy.md section 3): `:manual` is the
   default and today's behavior, a function `(fn [view])` is the
   embedder's rule, and `:lease` is reserved for the phase-2 deadline --
   refused, not implemented yet.  Anything else is refused with the
   supported values named."
  [policy]
  (cond
    (or (nil? policy) (= :manual policy)) :manual
    (fn? policy) policy
    :else
    (throw
      (ex-info
        (if (= :lease policy)
          "Yin REPL :link-policy :lease is not implemented yet"
          "Unknown Yin REPL :link-policy")
        {:link-policy policy
         :supported [:manual :fn]}))))

(defn create-state
  "Create the shell value.  `:primitives` is a host-supplied map merged over
   the REPL primitives; it is kept as `:extra-primitives` so every session
   rebuild — `(reset)`, `(vm …)` — installs it again.

   `content-store` (a `dao.jing` byte-store handle), `content-client` (a
   `dao.stream.rpc` client state on a connection whose far end serves
   content) and `name-env` (module name -> manifest address) compose the
   content pair and the name environment the linker interpreter serves
   `(require ...)` from (yin.vm.linker.interpreter/composition); with
   neither content source, a require stays `:pending` and says so.

   `:link-policy` is the session's pending-link rule
   (yin.repl.link-policy.md), kept beside `:link-source` so `(reset)` and
   `(vm ...)` preserve it: `:manual`, the default, ends a pending run
   only at `(abandon)`; a function `(fn [view])` is consulted when a
   require parks and after each re-check that leaves the run pending,
   answering `:keep`, `:abandon` or `{:abandon reason}`; `:lease` is
   reserved for phase 2 and refused, as is anything else, at assembly.

   `:admission` configures the signed-name source's in-process
   interpreter (`yin.vm.linker.interpreter/composition`'s option): by
   default `{}`, which trusts the own principal the composition declared
   alone; `{:trusted #{principal}}`, each `ed25519:<hex>`, trusts more;
   `:verify`, `:decision` and `:decision-medium` replace the default
   rule.
   `:external` runs no interpreter in process: the questions a require
   asks wait for an answer appended to the session's answer medium.

   `index-store` is the `dao.jing` byte store the code indexer publishes
   its covered indexes into (docs/design/yin.repl.dao.space-index.md); it
   outlives a session rebuild, and defaults to a fresh in-memory store.

   `index-store-spec` is the startup selection of that store
   (yin.repl.store): `:mem` — the default, today's behaviour — or
   `{:type :file :dir dir}`, the durable content log at
   `<dir>/content.jing`, opened under an exclusive directory lock with
   its HEAD read and the snapshot it names validated — a corrupt HEAD
   or snapshot refuses construction, and a second owner of the directory
   is refused naming it.  The spec is resolved and the store opened once
   here, never switched at runtime, and supplying it together with
   `index-store` (a handle injected directly) is refused.

   `:index-recovery` carries what the durable open recovered —
   `{:manifest <address or nil> :datoms <the validated snapshot or nil>}`
   — and the indexer is rehydrated from it here, before any evaluation
   is admitted (`yin.repl.index/rehydrate`): `q` answers the previous
   run's facts, which keep their own session tokens, while this process
   mints a new token for its own.  In durable mode `(reset)` and `(vm …)`
   carry the index across the rebuild; with the memory store they start
   an empty one, as they always have.

   A storage implementation past `:mem` and `{:type :file :dir dir}` is
   the composition's, never this namespace's
   (docs/design/yin.repl.dht-composition.md sections 2 and 3): it opens
   its own store and hands the engine the prepared `dao.jing` content
   handle as `:index-store`, what its open recovered as `:recovery`, the
   publication media it services as `:publication-media` and
   `:publication-policy`, and the link source it drives as
   `:link-source`.  The engine steps no transport and holds no node: a
   round publishes against the injected handle and never waits on a
   network, and a link the engine cannot serve itself stays pending for
   its composition to move (`yin.shell.linker/serve-links`).  Supplied
   together, `:link-source` wins over the generic content options, and
   `:index-store` wins over `:index-store-spec`.

   `:principals` are the public keys whose signed name assertions the
   reader honors, and `:follow` the principal ids whose published heads
   the composition follows.  Both are plain data on the link source; a
   `(require ...)` of a name that is absent while a followed principal
   has no installed head stays pending until that head is installed.
   `:publisher-key` is the session's own signing key `{:seed :public}`,
   whose principal joins `:principals` and is the `:own` the trust
   commands always honor.  It is signing material, not transport state:
   the engine reads only the principal off it, and never signs, resolves
   or announces.  A prepared `:link-source` already carries all three, so
   it wins and these are not read.

   `:custody` is an optional custody composition value
   (yin.vm.ucf.compose): the shell only carries it, as data, so the
   host's single step owner can advance it (yin.repl.main/step-all --
   the custody control step runs during hydration and through the
   bounded shutdown drain; the custody program step runs only while
   the shell is admitted and running).  Nothing in the shell reads or
   steps it; nil, the default, is today's behaviour.

   `:frontends` is the frontend catalog (`yang.frontend`) the session
   compiles through, composed by the host entry point (this namespace
   requires no frontend; see `yin.repl.frontends`).  Without it the catalog
   is empty and every compile answers `unavailable-parser`.  The session
   pins this immutable snapshot: installing into another catalog value
   never changes a live session.  `:lang` selects a frontend by id
   (`:yang/python`) or by `[id revision]`; a language keyword is not a
   selector. The default is the `:yang/clojure` frontend.
   one the catalog cannot answer is an `unavailable-parser` diagnostic,
   never a fallback to another frontend."
  ([] (create-state {}))
  ([{:keys [lang output-cursor output-stream vm-type primitives
            content-store content-client name-env link-policy index-store
            index-store-spec link-source recovery principals follow custody
            frontends admission publication-policy publication-media
            host-modules publisher-key]
     :or {lang :yang/clojure vm-type :semantic admission {}}}]
   (let [output-stream (or output-stream (make-output-medium!))
         output-cursor (or output-cursor (mint-cursor output-stream))
         shell-token (str (random-uuid))
         index-store-spec (cond
                            (and index-store index-store-spec)
                            (throw (ex-info
                                     (str "yin.repl/create-state takes one "
                                          "index store: :index-store-spec "
                                          "(mem or a file directory) or "

         ;; link source beside the handle and injects both; the engine

(defn pending-publication
  "The publication request this shell has emitted and no matching result
   has settled, or nil.  A composition reads it to know what it still
   owes the engine before it may report the round settled."
  [state]
  (index/pending-publication (:indexer state)))


(defn accept-publication-result
  "`state` after one local publication `result`
   (`{:op :publication-result :id :round :manifest :status :durability}`)
   the composition delivered.

   Only the result matching the pending request — identifier, round and
   manifest address together — settles it: `:published` promotes the
   frontier that request prepared and `:refused` preserves the previous
   published frontier, recording the round's failure under its reason.  A
   duplicate, stale or mismatched result promotes nothing, so a repeated
   or foreign result can never advance or regress the frontier.  A
   network dissemination result is not this: local durability alone
   settles a round."
  [state result]
  (update state :indexer index/accept-publication-result result))


(defn settle-publication
  "`state` after every publication result its composition has already
   appended is consumed.  A composition that services locally leaves
   nothing to consume; one with transport of its own calls this once it
   has delivered, before it reports the round settled."
  [state]
  (update state :indexer index/settle-publication))


(defn install-recovery
  "Install validated recovery data — `{:manifest address-or-nil :datoms
   datoms-or-nil}` — as the session's index history, answering the
   successor state.  The composition validates the manifest and every
   reachable index closure before it calls this, and calls it before
   evaluation is admitted: entity and transaction authority are derived
   from the history, and any saved live cursor is discarded, so the first
   subsequent publication reconstructs in full."

  (-> state
      (update :indexer index/rehydrate {:manifest manifest :datoms datoms})
      (assoc :index-recovery (or recovery {:manifest nil :datoms nil}))))


;; =============================================================================
  "Drive the code indexer's observer over `program-out`: it commits each
   forwarded packet as one transaction and publishes the covered indexes.
   It runs before the evaluator, so a program is indexed whether its VM
   returns, parks, or raises; the two observers meet only at the medium."

(defn- run-ast-index-stage
  "Drive the AST indexer's observer over `program-out`: it adds each
   forwarded packet's rows and occurrences to the session's `$ast` and
   `$occ` relations.  It runs before the evaluator for the same reason the
   code indexer does, and neither indexer reads the other."

(defn- with-index-notice
  "Append what the round's index steps lost, if anything, to its result
   text, one line per notice in the order given; the evaluation's own
   answer is unchanged."

  (if-let [notice (some->> (remove nil? notices) seq (str/join "\n"))]
    [state (if (str/blank? text) notice (str text "\n" notice))]

(defn- run-expander-stage
  "Drive the expander over `program-in` and drain its summary.  It expands
   each observed batch and appends the tree packet to `program-out`; a
   failed expansion forwards nothing, yet its cursor advances (yin.vm.macro.md
   decision 12).  Returns the state with the expander's progress and the
   drained `{:errors :forwarded}` summary."

        (macro/step {:observer (:observer state), :consumer (:expander state)})
        [expander summary] (macro/drain-errors consumer)]

(defn- run-evaluator-stage
  "Drive the evaluator's observer over `program-out`: it loads each
   expanded tree packet into the VM, runs it, and answers its value on the
   output medium.  The two stages meet only at `program-out`; neither calls
   the other."

(defn- format-expansion-errors

(defn- link-waiting?
  "True while `vm` parks on a link wait: the two link states `require`
   parks in, or the install it waits on (yin.vm.linker.md section 7.2).
   These are the reasons the shell's interpreter can move, so they are
   the ones a round drives before reporting the VM wedged."
  [vm]
  (boolean (some #(contains? #{:link-request :link-response :install}
                             (:reason %))
                 (:wait-set vm))))


(defn- carry-link-identity
  "The round's base VM with the link identity `used` has already minted
   carried forward: link ids `[origin counter]` and install-child origin
   tags are minted once and never reused on a pair (yin.vm.linker.md
   section 7.2), and the shell's rollback to the round's base -- whose
   counters never advanced -- must not let a later require or install
   mint an identity the pair has already answered."
  [base used]
  (let [n (max (or (:id-counter base) 0) (or (:id-counter used) 0))
        o (max (or (:origins base) 0) (or (:origins used) 0))]

      (pos? n) (assoc :id-counter n)
      (pos? o) (assoc :origins o))))


(defn- link-raise
  "The raise of a resumed link wait, carrying the identity the parked
   evaluation has minted so far -- the counters of the VM the raise
   interrupted, whose every earlier run is in them -- so a rollback
   cannot reuse it.  It carries the query interpreter's pair too: the
   requests it has answered stay answered when the shell rolls back.
   The linker successor carries every cursor and settled question."
  [error vm state]
  (ex-info (or (ex-message error) "Link failed")
           (assoc (or (ex-data error) {})
                  ::link-counter (:id-counter vm)
                  ::link-origins (:origins vm)
                  ::query-pair (:query-pair state)
                  ::linker (:linker state)
                  ::indexer (:indexer state))))


(defn- carry-served
  "`state` rolled back by a link raise, keeping what the interpreters
   already concluded: the query pair, the link pair past every request
   answered, the linker interpreter's past every question settled, and
   the indexer a name publication committed its envelopes through.  These
   are the settlement identities and cursors of a round that already had
   effects; nothing else survives the rollback, and no transport state
   crosses here — a composition's node is its own to retain across the
   engine's rollback (docs/design/yin.repl.dht-composition.md section 7)."
  [state d]
  (cond-> state
    (::query-pair d) (assoc :query-pair (::query-pair d))
    (::linker d) (assoc :linker (::linker d))
    (::indexer d) (assoc :indexer (::indexer d))))


(defn service-context
  "The explicit request data a composition answers a service call under:
   the requesting VM's primitives and module registry — the modules it
   linked are derived from it, never recorded — and the round.  The
   authority and any publisher key a signed service needs are the
   composition's to add; the engine holds neither
   (docs/design/yin.repl.dht-composition.md section 6)."
  [state vm]
  {:primitives (:primitives vm)
   :modules (:modules vm)
   :round (:round state)})

   composition can serve moves nothing here by construction

   something -- advanced a serve cursor, delivered a response or
   completed an install -- the fact the pending run's `:checks` resets

   raises as the VM's own, carrying the interrupted VM's minted
   identity.

   true, the first iteration runs the VM once without a round of its own.

   query interpreter (`yin.repl.query/serve`) answers from the session's

   link counts against `link-round-budget`; a query is answered in the
   round it is asked, so its rounds are bounded by `query-drive-budget`
   calls instead: a VM still waiting on a call once the drive has
   answered that many raises `query-call-limit-text` as its own error,
   the unanswered request abandoned with it."

         calls 0
         vm vm
         state state
         pending []
         progress? initial-progress
         initial? initial-progress]

        (throw (link-raise (ex-info query-call-limit-text

                                     :limit query-drive-budget})

(defn- fold-queued
  "Evaluate the lines retained while a require was pending, in the order
   they were typed, each exactly once, and join their texts.  A line that
   parks the shell on a require of its own stops the fold: the lines
   after it stay retained, in order, on the new `:pending-run`."

         text text
         [in & more :as queued] (seq queued)]

      (:pending-run state) [(update-in state [:pending-run :pending-lines]

(defn recheck-pending
  "One re-check of the shell's `:pending-run` without an input line --
   the step an unattended host drives at its own cadence
   (yin.repl.link-policy.md section 4): serve the interpreter, run the
   parked VM, and consult the link policy when the run is still
   pending.  A re-check that completes the run folds the retained lines
   exactly as a typed line's completion does.  Returns `[state text]`,
   `text` nil when nothing is pending.  It reads no clock and takes no
   callback; the host decides when to call it."
  [state]
  (if (:pending-run state)
    (recheck-pending* state nil false)
    [state nil]))


(defn recheck-on-tick
  "Advance one linker round the engine serves itself, carrying its
   successor before any VM run.  Progress resumes the pending driver
   before another round; otherwise only a generic completion event that
   matches the parked work rechecks the run, so an unrelated event is
   ignored and each completion resumes it once.  The two event shapes are
   `{:op :dependency :manifest address}` — a load the run waits on ended,
   under either status — and `{:op :principal :principal id}` — a head
   the run waits on was installed.  No transport keyword crosses inward:
   a composition translates its own events into these
   (`yin.shell.completion/completion-events`) and drives the linker round
   a signed source needs itself (`yin.shell.linker/serve-links`) before
   it calls this."
  [state events]
  (let [served (link/round-local (assoc (:linker state)
                                        :source (:link-source state)))
        state (if (= (:linker state) (:linker served))
                state
                (assoc state :linker (:linker served)))
        links (get-in state [:pending-run :links])
        waits (set (keep :manifest links))
        heads (set (mapcat :principals links))]
    (cond
      (and (:progress? served) (:pending-run state))
      (recheck-pending* state nil true)

      (some (fn [e]
              (or (and (= :dependency (:op e))
                       (contains? waits (:manifest e)))
                  (and (= :principal (:op e))
                       (contains? heads (:principal e)))))
            events)
      (recheck-pending state)

      :else [state nil])))


(defn- resume-pending
  "One bounded re-check of the shell's `:pending-run` behind a typed
   line: while the run stays pending the line is retained -- the parked
   VM owns the store a new evaluation would fork -- and it evaluates,
   in typing order and exactly once, when the link completes."
  [state trimmed parsed]
  (recheck-pending* state {:trimmed trimmed, :parsed parsed} false))

  [parsed]

(def output-capacity
  "Declared capacity of the composition-owned output medium, in elements."

(def ingress-capacity
  "Declared capacity of the composition-owned program medium, in elements.  The
   shell is the only appender and its one step owner serializes evaluation, so
   eviction can only follow a producer the composition does not make; a gap is
   therefore fatal to the current evaluation rather than a normal operating
   condition."
  4096)


(def drain-budget
  "Maximum elements one output drain reads.  It equals the output capacity,
   so one drain reaches every element the medium still holds, the round's
   result included."
  output-capacity)


(def gap-budget
  "Maximum `gap` answers one output drain accepts.  A gap is not an element,
   so it is counted apart from `drain-budget`: a gap never costs the drain
   an element, and the drain stays total against a transport that could
   answer `gap` repeatedly."
  4096)


(def link-round-budget
  "How many serve-and-run rounds one evaluation drives while its VM waits
   on a link (yin.vm.linker.md sections 6.3 and 7.2).  A round serves the
   interpreter once and runs the VM once; a local content source answers
   within a few, so the budget is reached only by a link that stays
   `:pending`, which the shell then reports as its own non-blocking state
   instead of wedging on."
  40)


(def query-row-limit
  "The most rows one `dao.space.query/q` answer may carry: members of a
   relation or collection, one for a scalar or tuple.  An answer is a
   value the REPL prints whole, so a result past a thousand rows is a
   query to narrow rather than one to read; a `def` of ordinary size
   projects to tens or hundreds of facts, so every fact of a few
   definitions still fits."
  1000)


(def query-byte-limit
  "The most canonical CBOR bytes one `dao.space.query/q` answer may
   encode to, 256 KiB.  Rows bound the count, not the size: one row can
   hold a long string literal.  The byte bound keeps every answer on the
   bounded call-out a fixed size, so the medium's retention is bounded by
   and the run parks for that composition to move.  Returns
   `[state vm pending progress?]`, `pending` the links the interpreter
   reported `:pending`, and `progress?` true when a round moved
   something -- advanced a serve cursor, delivered a response or
   completed an install -- the fact the pending run's `:checks` resets
   on (yin.repl.link-policy.md section 3.1).  A refused or lost link
   raises as the VM's own, carrying the interrupted VM's minted
   identity.

   `initial-progress` records progress from the caller's round.  When
   true, the first iteration runs the VM once without a round of its own.

   A VM waiting on a `dao.space.query/q` call is driven the same way: the
   query interpreter (`yin.repl.query/serve`) answers from the session's
   indexer and the VM runs on.  Only a round the VM spends waiting on a
   link counts against `link-round-budget`; a query is answered in the
   round it is asked, so its rounds are bounded by `query-drive-budget`
   calls instead: a VM still waiting on a call once the drive has
   answered that many raises `query-call-limit-text` as its own error,
   the unanswered request abandoned with it."
  [state vm initial-progress]
  (loop [i 0
         calls 0
         vm vm
         state state
         pending []
         progress? initial-progress
         initial? initial-progress]
    (let [link? (link-waiting? vm)
          query? (query/waiting? vm)]
      (cond
        (or (vm/halted? vm) (not (or link? query?)) (>= i link-round-budget))
        [state vm pending progress?]

        (and query? (>= calls query-drive-budget))
        (throw (link-raise (ex-info query-call-limit-text
                                    {:reason :yin.repl.query/call-limit
                                     :limit query-drive-budget})
                           vm
                           (update state :query-pair query/abandon-requests)))

        :else
        (let [served (when (and link? (not initial?))
                       (link/round-local (assoc (:linker state)
                                                :source (:link-source state))))
              state (cond-> state
                      served (assoc :linker (:linker served)))
              answered (when query?
                         (query/serve {:pair (:query-pair state)
                                       :indexer (:indexer state)
                                       :ast-indexer (:ast-indexer state)
                                       :limits {:row-limit query-row-limit
                                                :byte-limit query-byte-limit}
                                       :budget (min query-serve-budget
                                                    (- query-drive-budget
                                                       calls))}))
              state (cond-> state
                      answered (assoc :query-pair (:pair answered)
                                      :indexer (:indexer answered)))
              pending (if (seq (:pending served)) (:pending served) pending)]
          (if (or initial? (:progress? served)
                  (:progress? answered))
            (let [vm' (try (vm/run vm)
                           (catch #?(:cljd Object :clj Exception :cljs js/Error)
                                  error
                             (throw (link-raise error vm state))))]
              (recur (if link? (inc i) i)
                     (+ calls (:answered answered 0))
                     vm'
                     state
                     pending
                     true
                     false))
            [state vm pending progress?]))))))


(defn- tokenize
  "Answer the halted VM's value on the output medium under `state`'s
   round, as the evaluator runner does for a program it runs itself.  A
   resumed require halts outside the observer loop, so the shell emits
   its token here."
  [state vm]
  ((make-runner (:output-stream state) (round-id state)) vm))


(defn- pending-text
  [pending]
  (if (seq pending)
    (str ";; require pending: "
         (str/join ", " (map (fn [p]
                               (str (pr-str (:name p))
                                    " (link " (pr-str (:yin.link/id p))
                                    (when (:admission p)
                                      ", awaiting admission")
                                    ")"))
                             pending))
         "); lines typed meanwhile run when it completes, (abandon) gives"
         " up\n")
    (str ";; require still pending; lines typed meanwhile run when it"
         " completes, (abandon) gives up\n")))


(defn- dropped-lines-text
  [n]
  (when (pos? n)
    (str ";; dropped " n " line" (when (> n 1) "s")
         " typed while the require was pending\n")))


(def ^:private policy-abandon-text
  "The message a policy-driven abandon prints, in the shape of the
   new expander holds only the standard forms.  A require still pending
   on the old VM is dropped with it: its link pair is the session's, and
   the new session answers from its own.

   Over a durable store the code index is not the session's to drop: the
   new indexer continues the old one's log, entity allocation, and
   published manifest (`yin.repl.index/carry-over`), so a rebuild never
   resets `t`.  Over the memory store it starts empty, as it always has."
  [state vm-type]
  (merge state
         (cond-> (make-session vm-type (:output-stream state)
                               (merge (selected-primitives (:frontends state)
                                                           (:lang state))
                                      (:extra-primitives state))
                               (:shell-token state)
                               (:index-store state)
                               (:link-source state)
                               (cond-> (:publication state)
                                 (get-in state [:indexer :publication-media])
                                 (assoc :media
                                        (get-in state
                                                [:indexer :publication-media])))
                               (:host-modules state))
           (store/durable? (:index-store state))
           (update :indexer index/carry-over (:indexer state)))
         {:vm-type vm-type
          :ingress-loss? false
          :last-value nil
          :last-value-2 nil
          :last-value-3 nil
          :frontend-session nil
          :pending-run nil}))


(defn- configure-admission
  "Apply session configuration to the linker, retaining its live state."
  [state admission]
  (let [linker (link/reconfigure (:linker state) admission)]
    (assoc state :admission admission :linker linker
           :link-source (:source linker))))


(defn- trust-command
  [state command args]
  (try
    (let [p (first args)]
      (when-not (and (= 1 (count args)) (string? p)
                     (str/starts-with? p "ed25519:"))
        (throw (ex-info "Expected one ed25519:<64 hex> principal id" {})))
      (let [p (config/parse-trust p)
            admission (if (= :external (:admission state))
        (and form (ast-map? form)) (eval-program state form)
        forms (eval-compiled state (compile-input state trimmed forms))
        (forms-input? state) [state (format-error (:error parsed))]
        :else (eval-compiled state (compile-source state trimmed))))
    (catch #?(:cljd Object :clj Exception :cljs js/Error) error
      (let [[state' output-text] (drain-output state)]
        [state' (str output-text (format-error error))]))))


(defn- fold-queued
  "Evaluate the lines retained while a require was pending, in the order
   they were typed, each exactly once, and join their texts.  A line that
   parks the shell on a require of its own stops the fold: the lines
   after it stay retained, in order, on the new `:pending-run`."
  [[state text] queued]
  (loop [state state
         text text
         [in & more :as queued] (seq queued)]
    (cond
      (empty? queued) [state text]
      (:pending-run state) [(update-in state [:pending-run :pending-lines]
                                       (fnil into []) queued)
                            text]
      :else (let [[state' text'] (eval-parsed* state
                                               (:trimmed in)
                                               (:parsed in))]
              (recur state' (str text "\n" text') more)))))


(defn- recheck-pending*
  "One bounded re-check of the shell's `:pending-run`: serve the
   interpreter, run the parked VM, and either answer its value -- the
   round the require began in finally completes, and the lines retained
   while it was pending, then `input`, evaluate against it -- consult
   the link policy when the re-check leaves the run pending, `:checks`
   counting this pending run's re-checks that made no progress and
   resetting on one that did, or, when the re-check raised the link's
   refusal, return the shell to the round's base with the error as text
   and evaluate `input` there.  `input` is nil for the host's
   `recheck-pending`, which evaluates no line of its own."
  [state input initial-progress]
  (let [parked (:pending-run state)]
    (try
      (let [[state' vm' pending progress?] (drive-links state (:vm parked)
                                                        initial-progress)]
        (if (vm/halted? vm')
          (let [vm'' (engine/restore-initial-env (:env (:base parked)) vm')
                [st text] (finalize-eval state
                                         (cond-> (assoc state' :vm vm'')
                                           (:frontend parked)
                                           (assoc ::frontend
                                                  (:frontend parked)))
                                         (tokenize state' vm''))]
            (fold-queued [(assoc st :vm vm'' :pending-run nil) text]
                         (cond-> (vec (:pending-lines parked))
                           input (conj input))))
          (let [checks (if progress? 0 (inc (or (:checks parked) 0)))
                parked' (cond-> (assoc parked
                                       :vm vm'
                                       :links pending
                                       :checks checks)
                          input (update :pending-lines
                                        (fnil conj []) input))
                [st text] (drain-output (assoc state'
                                               :vm vm'
                                               :pending-run parked'))]
            (consult-link-policy st text (pending-text pending)))))
      (catch #?(:cljd Object :clj Exception :cljs js/Error) error
        (let [[st text] (drain-output state)
              d (ex-data error)]
          (fold-queued
            [(carry-served (assoc st
                                  :vm (query/discard-answers
                                        (carry-link-identity
                                          (:base parked)
                                          {:id-counter (::link-counter d)
                                           :origins (::link-origins d)})
                                        (:query-pair st))
                                  :pending-run nil)
                           d)
             (str text
                  (format-error error)
                  (dropped-lines-text (count (:pending-lines parked))))]
            (cond-> [] input (conj input))))))))


(defn recheck-pending
  "One re-check of the shell's `:pending-run` without an input line --
   the step an unattended host drives at its own cadence
   (yin.repl.link-policy.md section 4): serve the interpreter, run the
   parked VM, and consult the link policy when the run is still
   pending.  A re-check that completes the run folds the retained lines
   exactly as a typed line's completion does.  Returns `[state text]`,
   `text` nil when nothing is pending.  It reads no clock and takes no
   callback; the host decides when to call it."
  [state]
  (if (:pending-run state)
    (recheck-pending* state nil false)
    [state nil]))

(defn open
  "Open the store `spec` names and keep it plain: `:mem` (or nil) is a
   fresh in-memory `dao.jing` store; `{:type :file :dir dir}` is the
   durable directory store at `dir` (dao.space.store/open): exclusive,
   validating, its HEAD writer, recovery and lock on the handle.  A spec
   this build cannot open is refused with its reason; a `dht:<dir>` spec
   is opened by yin.repl.dht, which composes its node over the same
   durable store."
  [spec]
  (let [checked (checked-spec spec)]
    (case (if (map? checked) (:type checked) checked)
      :mem (jing.mem/create-content-mem)
      :file (durable/open (:dir checked))
      :dht (throw (ex-info (str "a dht:<dir> store is opened by "
                                "yin.repl.dht/open, which composes its node")
                           {:spec (dissoc checked :bind!)})))))

   starting an empty one (dao.space.store/durable?)."

(deftest the-suffix-folded-is-exactly-the-unpublished-suffix
  ;; Expected suffix length (spec section 8): with a valid frontier, a
  ;; round folds exactly the records past the retained cursor -- here
  ;; two new transactions, read as two hits and one blocked read, with
  ;; no reopening of the covered prefix.
  (doseq [kind fixture/backend-kinds]
    (testing (str kind)
      (fixture/call-with-backend
        kind
        (fn [backend]
          (let [{:keys [writer observer]} (small-medium 16)
                reads (atom [])
                initial (update (repl.index/make-indexer
                                  {:observer observer :session-token "suffix"
                                   :content-store (:handle backend)
                                   :publish-opts {:branching-factor 4}})
                                :local #(->CountingLocal % reads))
                _ (stream/append! writer (literal-packet 1))
                ix1 (repl.index/step initial 1)

                ix3 (repl.index/step ix2 3)

            (is (not-any? #(= [:cursor :dao.stream/oldest] %) @reads)

(deftest a-settled-frontier-is-not-settled-twice
  ;; Duplicate or stale settlement (spec section 4): only the round that
  ;; materialized and read back its manifest promotes the frontier, and
  ;; only once.  Re-stepping with nothing new requests no second
  ;; publication; a refused name publication commits its transaction
  ;; without promoting the frontier past it.
  (doseq [kind fixture/backend-kinds]
    (testing (str kind)
      (fixture/call-with-backend
        kind
        (fn [backend]
          (let [{:keys [writer observer]} (small-medium 16)
                heads (atom [])
                initial (repl.index/make-indexer
                          {:observer observer :session-token "settle-once"
                           :content-store (:handle backend)
                           :publication-media (fixture/head-media
                                                (fn [m] (swap! heads conj m)))
                           :publish-opts {:branching-factor 4}})
                _ (stream/append! writer (literal-packet 1))
                ix1 (repl.index/step initial 1)
                f1 (fixture/frontier ix1)
                again (repl.index/step ix1 2)]
            (is (= [(:manifest-address f1)] @heads)
                "the successful round requested durable publication once")
            (testing "re-stepping a settled frontier settles nothing again"
              (is (= (:materialization f1)
                     (:materialization (fixture/frontier again))))
              (is (= 1 (count @heads))))
            (testing "a refused publication result cannot settle its round"
              (let [refused (repl.index/commit-names
                              (assoc ix1 :publication-media (fixture/refusing-media))
                              [] 3)
                    fr (fixture/frontier refused)]
                (is (= :publish (get-in refused [:failure :stage])))
                (is (= (:manifest-address f1) (:manifest-address fr)))
                (is (= 1 (:published fr)))
                (is (= 2 (:transactions fr))
                    "the transaction committed; only its promotion was refused")
                (is (false? (:published? (:status fr))))))))))))

(defn close-backend!
  "Close a backend's handle (releasing a file backend's directory lock)
   and remove its scratch directory.  Idempotent in effect: a second
   close of a content handle is refused by nothing here."
  [{:keys [handle dir]}]
  (when-let [close! (:close-fn handle)]
    (try (close!) (catch #?(:cljd Object :clj Exception :cljs :default) _ nil)))
  (cleanup-dir! dir)
  nil)


(defn call-with-backend
  "Open backend `kind`, call `(f backend)`, and close the backend even
   when `f` throws.  Answers `f`'s value; anything a test needs from the
   store must be read inside `f`, before the close."
  ([kind f] (call-with-backend kind {} f))
  ([kind opts f]
   (let [backend (open-backend kind opts)]
     (try (f backend)
          (finally (close-backend! backend))))))

;; The common test constructor (Gate B's injection point)
