(defn create-state
  "A shell over `backend`'s explicitly injected `dao.jing` handle, plus
   `opts` for `yin.repl.frontends/create-state` (`:vm-type`,
   `:content-store`, `:name-env`, ...).  This is Gate B's constructor:
   the proof never relies on the default memory construction, and no
   `:index-store-spec` -- the only path that can name DHT -- is used."
  ([backend] (create-state backend {}))
  ([backend opts]
   (repl.frontends/create-state (merge {:index-store (:handle backend)} opts))))


(defn call-with-state
  "Open backend `kind`, build a shell over it with `opts`, call
   `(f state backend)`, and close the backend afterwards."
  ([kind f] (call-with-state kind {} f))
  ([kind opts f]
   (call-with-backend kind (fn [backend] (f (create-state backend opts) backend)))))


;; =============================================================================
;; Publication observation: the composition-side interpreter (Step 1 form)
;; =============================================================================

(defn- recording-head-fn
  "The Step 1 composition interpreter over one backend's `:head-fn`:
   each call mints the next section 4 correlation (`:id` and `:round`
   are the call sequence, because today's seam carries only the
   manifest) and appends exactly one result record to `log` -- after
   the HEAD write's outcome is known, so a refusal is never recorded
   as a success.  While `refuse?` holds true the write is refused
   without delegating.  The write's exception always propagates."
  [log sequence inner durability refuse?]
  (fn [manifest-address]
    (let [n (swap! sequence inc)
          request (publication-request n n manifest-address)]
      (if (and refuse? @refuse?)
        (do (swap! log conj (publication-result request :refused
                                                durability "HEAD refused"))
            (throw (ex-info "HEAD refused" {})))
        (try
          (when inner (inner manifest-address))
          (swap! log conj (publication-result request :published durability))
          (catch #?(:cljd Object :clj Exception :cljs :default) e
            (swap! log conj (publication-result
                              request :refused durability
                              (or (ex-message e) "HEAD refused")))
            (throw e)))))))


(defn publication-requests
  "The section 4 requests a result `log` answers, oldest first: each
   result's `:id` / `:round` / `:manifest` projected back to its
   `{:op :publish ...}` request."
  [log-values]
  (mapv #(publication-request (:id %) (:round %) (:manifest %)) log-values))


(defn observed-backend
  "Backend whose durable-publication results are recorded in `log` (an
   atom of vectors): each `:head-fn` call appends one
   `{:op :publication-result :id :round :manifest :status :durability}`
   record (`:refused` results also carry `:reason`).  A memory backend
   has no `:head-fn` today; observing one installs a recording writer
   that acknowledges local completion in memory only -- it never makes
   the ephemeral store claim persistence."
  [backend log]
  (let [handle (:handle backend)]
    (assoc backend :handle
           (assoc handle :head-fn
                  (recording-head-fn log (atom 0) (:head-fn handle)
                                     (:durability backend) nil)))))


(defn failable-backend
  "Like `observed-backend`, but while `fail?` (an atom) holds true the
   HEAD write is refused instead of delegating: the log gains a
   `:refused` result and the caller sees the refusal throw.  Tests read
   attempts and outcomes from the same log: `:status` distinguishes
   them, and only `:published` manifests may appear as the promoted
   frontier."
  [backend log fail?]
  (let [handle (:handle backend)]
    (assoc backend :handle
           (assoc handle :head-fn
                  (recording-head-fn log (atom 0) (:head-fn handle)
                                     (:durability backend) fail?)))))


;; =============================================================================
;; Frontier reading (spec section 8, Frontier gate)
;; =============================================================================

(defn stream-values
  "Every value currently on stream `s`, read from its oldest cursor."
  [s]
  (loop [cursor (:dao.stream/cursor (stream/cursor s :dao.stream/oldest))
         acc []]
    (let [r (stream/next s cursor)]
      (if (= :dao.stream/ok (:dao.stream/outcome r))
        (recur (:dao.stream/cursor r) (conj acc (:dao.stream/value r)))
        acc))))


(defn transactions

(defn- drive-links
  "Serve the linker interpreter and run the parked VM alternately, at most
   `link-round-budget` rounds, while `vm` waits on a link.  A round that
   moves nothing ends the drive: a link whose content source cannot
   answer will not answer by waiting longer.  A source only its
   composition can serve moves nothing here by construction
   (`yin.vm.linker.interpreter/round-local`), so the drive ends at once
   and the run parks for that composition to move.  Returns
   `[state vm pending progress?]`, `pending` the links the interpreter
   reported `:pending`, and `progress?` true when a round moved
   something -- advanced a serve cursor, delivered a response or
   completed an install -- the fact the pending run's `:checks` resets
   on (yin.repl.link-policy.md section 3.1).  A refused or lost link
   raises as the VM's own, carrying the interrupted VM's minted
   identity.

   `initial-progress` records progress from the caller's round.  When
   true, the first iteration runs the VM once without a round of its own.

   A VM waiting on a `dao.space.query/q` call is driven the same way: the
   query interpreter (`yin.repl.query/serve`) answers from the session's
   indexer and the VM runs on.  Only a round the VM spends waiting on a
   link counts against `link-round-budget`; a query is answered in the
   round it is asked, so its rounds are bounded by `query-drive-budget`
   calls instead: a VM still waiting on a call once the drive has
   answered that many raises `query-call-limit-text` as its own error,
   the unanswered request abandoned with it."
  [state vm initial-progress]
  (loop [i 0
         calls 0
         vm vm
         state state
         pending []
         progress? initial-progress
         initial? initial-progress]
    (let [link? (link-waiting? vm)
          query? (query/waiting? vm)]
      (cond
        (or (vm/halted? vm) (not (or link? query?)) (>= i link-round-budget))
        [state vm pending progress?]

        (and query? (>= calls query-drive-budget))
        (throw (link-raise (ex-info query-call-limit-text
                                    {:reason :yin.repl.query/call-limit
                                     :limit query-drive-budget})
                           vm
                           (update state :query-pair query/abandon-requests)))

        :else
        (let [served (when (and link? (not initial?))
                       (link/round-local (assoc (:linker state)
                                                :source (:link-source state))))
              state (cond-> state
                      served (assoc :linker (:linker served)))
              answered (when query?
                         (query/serve {:pair (:query-pair state)
                                       :indexer (:indexer state)
                                       :ast-indexer (:ast-indexer state)
                                       :limits {:row-limit query-row-limit
                                                :byte-limit query-byte-limit}
                                       :budget (min query-serve-budget
                                                    (- query-drive-budget
                                                       calls))}))
              state (cond-> state
                      answered (assoc :query-pair (:pair answered)
                                      :indexer (:indexer answered)))
              pending (if (seq (:pending served)) (:pending served) pending)]
          (if (or initial? (:progress? served)
                  (:progress? answered))
            (let [vm' (try (vm/run vm)
                           (catch #?(:cljd Object :clj Exception :cljs js/Error)
                                  error
                             (throw (link-raise error vm state))))]
              (recur (if link? (inc i) i)
                     (+ calls (:answered answered 0))
                     vm'
                     state
                     pending
                     true
                     false))
            [state vm pending progress?]))))))

(defn serve
  "One serve round of the engine's local query interpreter over `pair`:
   answer every request its cursor has not consumed, from `indexer` and
   `ast-indexer` as they stand now, at most `budget` of them.  A response
   is appended before the cursor moves past its request; one the call-out
   refuses leaves the request to be re-read.

   A `foreign-request?` under `registered-ops` ends the round and stays
   unread, answered under `:deferred`: the composition that registered its
   module reads it from the same cursor and answers it there.  An unknown
   operation is answered with a refusal on the spot, preserving local
   request/response completion.

   Returns `{:pair pair :indexer indexer :progress? bool :answered n
   :deferred request-or-nil}`, `n` the responses appended."
  [{:keys [pair indexer ast-indexer limits budget registered-ops]}]
  (loop [pair pair
         indexer indexer
         remaining budget
         progress? false
         answered 0]
    (let [done (fn [deferred]
                 {:pair pair, :indexer indexer, :progress? progress?,
                  :answered answered, :deferred deferred})
          r (when (pos? remaining)
              (stream/next (:call-in pair) (:cursor pair)))]
      (if-not (= :dao.stream/ok (:dao.stream/outcome r))
        (done nil)
        (let [request (:dao.stream/value r)]
          (cond
            (and registered-ops (foreign-request? registered-ops request))
            (done request)

            (not (apply2/request? request))
            (recur (assoc pair :cursor (:dao.stream/cursor r))
                   indexer (dec remaining) true answered)

            :else
            (let [response (answer indexer ast-indexer limits request)]
              (if (= :dao.stream/ok
                     (:dao.stream/outcome
                       (apply2/put-response! (:call-out pair) response)))
                (recur (assoc pair :cursor (:dao.stream/cursor r))
                       indexer (dec remaining) true (inc answered))
                (done nil)))))))))

         (if tree
           (str "\n\nExpanded rows:\n" (format-value tree))
           (str "\n\nExpansion error:\n" (format-value error)))
         "\n\nEvents:\n" (format-value (second log)))))


(defn- rebuild-session
  "Replace the VM, the expander, and their media, attachments, and
   observers.  The value history is cleared with them: a closure in `*1`
   names a code segment the old VM held, which the new one does not.  The
   new expander holds only the standard forms.  A require still pending
   on the old VM is dropped with it: its link pair is the session's, and
   the new session answers from its own.

   Over a durable store the code index is not the session's to drop: the
   new indexer continues the old one's log, entity allocation, and
   published manifest (`yin.repl.index/carry-over`), so a rebuild never
   resets `t`.  Over the memory store it starts empty, as it always has."
  [state vm-type]
  (merge state
         (cond-> (make-session vm-type (:output-stream state)
                               (merge (selected-primitives (:frontends state)
                                                           (:lang state))
                                      (:extra-primitives state))
                               (:shell-token state)
                               (:index-store state)
                               (:link-source state)
                               (cond-> (:publication state)
                                 (get-in state [:indexer :publication-media])
                                 (assoc :media
                                        (get-in state
                                                [:indexer :publication-media])))
                               (:host-modules state))
           (store/durable? (:index-store state))
           (update :indexer index/carry-over (:indexer state)))
         {:vm-type vm-type
          :ingress-loss? false
          :last-value nil
          :last-value-2 nil
          :last-value-3 nil
          :frontend-session nil
          :pending-run nil}))

(defn carry-over
  "A rebuilt session's fresh `indexer`, continuing `previous`'s index: its
   transaction log, entity allocation, counts, published manifest, and
   live allocator/verified materialization successors.
   `(reset)` and VM selection over a durable store use it, so a rebuild
   never resets `t` or entity allocation and `q` keeps answering the
   published index; the observer is the new session's, and a lost or
   failed indexer is recovered by the rebuild as it is today."

                                :published-payloads :manifest-address
                                :allocator :materialization :unwritten])))

(defn- evaluate
  [db view query inputs limits]
  (bounded #(query/collect (apply query/q query (view db) inputs)) limits))


(defn answer
  "The response to one call-pair `request`, answered from `indexer`, and
   from `ast-indexer` for a query naming `$ast` or `$occ`, under `limits`
   (`{:row-limit n :byte-limit n}`).  Without an AST indexer such a query
   is refused."
  ([indexer limits request]
   (answer indexer nil limits request))
  ([indexer ast-indexer limits request]
   (let [id (apply2/request-id request)
         [query & more] (apply2/request-args request)
         answer (cond
                  (not= op (apply2/request-op request))
                  (refusal :dao.stream.apply/unknown-operation
                           "No handler for operation"
                           nil)

                  (nil? (encoded-size (apply2/request-args request)))
                  (invalid (str "q takes portable Yin data only: nil, booleans,"
                                " numbers, strings, keywords, symbols, and"
                                " vectors, lists, sets and maps of them"))

                  (not (or (vector? query) (map? query)))
                  (invalid (str "q expects a query vector or map, got "
                                (pr-str query)))

                  :else
                  (let [split (split-args query more)
                        [inputs options] (when-not (refused? split) split)
                        view (when-not (refused? split) (view-of options))
                        db (when-not (or (refused? split) (refused? view))
                             (snapshot indexer))
                        sources (when-not (or (refused? split) (refused? view)
                                              (refused? db))
                                  (ast-relations ast-indexer
                                                 (ast-patterns query)))]
                    (cond
                      (refused? split) split
                      (refused? view) view
                      (refused? db) db
                      (refused? sources) sources
                      :else (evaluate db view (with-index query)
                                      (into sources inputs) limits))))]
     (response id answer))))

   call-out from the newest position of `pair`'s call-out.  The base's
   own cursor stopped where its round began; every response since
   answers a call of the abandoned run, which no call of the base can
   claim, and a failed round that made more calls than the medium holds

(ns yin.repl.require-test
  "M5 (docs/design/yin.vm.linker.md sections 6.1, 7.2 and 9): `(require
   'foo)` typed at the prompt of `yin.repl` reaches the shell's linker
   interpreter, links the module's manifest over the content pair,
   installs through the child phases, and resumes with the export bound
   -- on every backend the shell supports.  The content source is an
   in-process `dao.jing` store served behind the content interpreter
   (`dao.jing.content/serve-step`); the link pair is the session's, so a
   link whose source cannot answer surfaces as the shell's own
   `:pending` state, and `(abandon)` gives it up.

   Modules are minted four ways (tree, semantic vector, H, R) with
   derivation records under the profiles this linker re-lowers, exactly
   as `yin.vm.linker-manifest-test` mints its corpus; the shell requests
   the format its own kernel names.  The closed corpus links on all four
   backends; the store-carrying one closes over a module binding, which
   the tree scanner conservatively retains (section 4.1), so it links on
   the two backends whose scanners discharge it -- the H/R pair the
   criterion names.  Input lines stay readable by every host's
   non-evaluating reader, so quoted names are spelled `(quote ...)`."
  (:require [clojure.string :as str]
            [clojure.test :refer [deftest is testing]]
            [dao.jing.mem :as mem]
            [dao.stream :as stream]
            [dao.stream.ringbuffer :as ring]
            [yin.repl :as repl]
            [yin.repl.fixture :as fixture]
            [yin.repl.frontends :as repl.frontends]
            [yin.vm :as vm]
            [yin.vm.engine :as engine]
            [yin.vm.debruijn-code-test :as b0]
            [yin.vm.linker.interpreter :as link]
            [yin.vm.linker.publish :as publish]
            [yin.vm.test-utils :as tu]))


;; =============================================================================
;; AST helpers and the module corpora
;; =============================================================================

(defn- lit
  [x]
  {:type :literal, :value x})


(defn- v
  [n]
  {:type :variable, :name n})


(defn- lam
  [params body]
  {:type :lambda, :params params, :body body})


(defn- app
  [f & args]
  {:type :application, :operator f, :operands (vec args)})


(defn- def!
  [k val]
  (app (v 'yin/def) (lit k) val))


(defn- then
  "`first` for its effect, then `second`: `((fn [_] second) first)`."
  [first-ast second-ast]
  (app (lam '[_] second-ast) first-ast))


(defn- progn
  [& asts]
  (reduce then asts))


(def closed-module
  "`(yin/def f (fn [] (+ 40 2)))`: one export, one retained free name.
   The shell corpus: it links on every backend the shell supports."
  (def! 'f (lam [] (app (v '+) (lit 40) (lit 2)))))


(def closed-exports
  #{'f})


(def closed-value
  "What the export answers: B0's own baseline for the corpus."
  (app (v '+) (lit 40) (lit 2)))


(def store-module
  "A module binding `n`, and an export reading it, so the install
   carries a store snapshot across the child-to-parent boundary.  The
   tree scanner conservatively retains the in-body read of `n`
   (section 4.1) and a manifest declares only primitives and requires,
   so this one links on semantic, stack and register, whose scans
   discharge the read."
  (progn (def! 'n (lit 40))
         (def! 'f (lam [] (app (v '+) (v 'n) (lit 2))))))


(def store-exports
  #{'n 'f})


(def plus-profile
  "The published profile address of `+`, the one free name both corpora
   retain."
  (get-in vm/primitives ['+ :yin.k/profile]))

(defn- next-entity-id
  "One greater than the greatest entity or metadata-entity id `datoms`
   use, never below `datom/first-user-id`."
  [datoms]
  (reduce (fn [next-e [e _a _v _t m]]
            (cond-> next-e
              (integer? e) (max (inc e))
              (integer? m) (max (inc m))))
          datom/first-user-id
          datoms))


(defn rehydrate
  "Seed a fresh indexer from a recovered durable snapshot, `{:manifest
   address :datoms [...]}` (yin.repl.store's `:recovery`), before any
   evaluation is admitted.  Its log becomes a fresh complete-retention
   memory log holding the recovered datoms as transaction records, one
   per original `t` in ascending order, each datom and its `t` preserved,
   so a new transactor derives the next `t` from it. Entity
   allocation resumes one past the greatest restored entity or metadata
   id.  The manifest is the published one, covering every restored
   transaction, so `q` answers from it before anything new is evaluated.
   Restored facts keep their original session tokens and round metadata:
   they are the datoms as committed.  A recovery without a manifest is an
   empty index. Live allocation and publication successors are always
   discarded, including any stale or foreign cursor: the first subsequent
   publication takes the full reconstruction path and derives a new cursor
   from this log, never from a saved process checkpoint."
  [indexer {:keys [manifest datoms]}]
  (if (nil? manifest)
    (assoc indexer :allocator nil :materialization nil)
    (let [log (memory-log)
          by-t (group-by index/datom-t datoms)
          ts (sort (keys by-t))]
      (doseq [t ts]
        (let [answer (stream/append! log {:dao.space/transaction
                                          {:t t, :datoms (vec (get by-t t))}})]
          (when-not (= :dao.stream/ok (:dao.stream/outcome answer))
            (throw (ex-info "the recovered snapshot could not be rehydrated"
                            {:t t, :outcome answer})))))
      (assoc indexer
             :local log
             :next-e (next-entity-id datoms)
             :transactions (count ts)
             :published (count ts)
             :allocator nil
             :materialization nil

item.text: The JVM smoke checks confirmed the failures: requiring `yin.repl` loads both DHT namespaces; a registered `yin.head/heads` call returns `unknown-operation`; and a delivered link response leaves the VM parked until the progress flag is supplied. A publication check also showed a queued success being discarded when the next commit overwrote its pending request. These block Step 2 sign-off.

**Recommendation: withhold Step 2 sign-off.** I reviewed the uncommitted changes against `71dd717da07ce23a744aed4fe10ccbeabeae9333`. The extraction makes useful progress, but neither part of the §9 exit condition—“Engine owns no DHT state or dependency; local synchronous behavior preserved”—is fully satisfied.

The following findings block approval.

1. **[P1] The engine still loads the DHT implementation.**  
   `yin.repl` still requires `yin.vm.linker.interpreter`, whose [namespace imports](/Users/sto/workspace/datomworld-yin-repl-dht/src/cljc/yin/vm/linker/interpreter.cljc:35) include `dao.space.dht` and `yin.vm.linker.dht`. `round-local` adds a node-free wrapper but does not separate the dependency closure, which §2 explicitly requires.

   **Verified:** in a fresh JVM, requiring only `yin.repl` left both `dao.space.dht` and `dao.jing.dht` loaded. Split the generic linker machinery from DHT serving, or move interpreter ownership entirely to composition.

2. **[P1] Publication still invokes an injected HEAD callback inside the engine.**  
   [Engine construction](/Users/sto/workspace/datomworld-yin-repl-dht/src/cljc/yin/repl.cljc:985) extracts `:head-fn` into `:publication-media`. The [indexer](/Users/sto/workspace/datomworld-yin-repl-dht/src/cljc/yin/repl/index.cljc:475) then calls `service-local!`, which [invokes that function directly](/Users/sto/workspace/datomworld-yin-repl-dht/src/cljc/yin/repl/publication.cljc:89). Adding request/result records around this call does not establish the composition-owned interpreter required by §§3–4.

   Store selection also remains in `create-state` through `store/checked-spec` and `store/open`; reset retention still uses `store/durable?`. Composition must own these decisions, pump publication requests, and deliver results before reporting local evaluation settled.

3. **[P1] Registered composition calls are consumed and refused by the engine.**  
   [Local query serving](/Users/sto/workspace/datomworld-yin-repl-dht/src/cljc/yin/repl/query.cljc:639) defers requests only when `registered-ops` is supplied. The [engine caller](/Users/sto/workspace/datomworld-yin-repl-dht/src/cljc/yin/repl.cljc:1448) never supplies it, and no other code wires it.

   **Reproduced:** after constructing an engine with `shell.query/registrations` and requiring `yin.head`, `(yin.head/heads)` returns `:dao.stream.apply/unknown-operation`. Its request has already been consumed before composition can answer. Carry the registered operation identities through the generic service contract while preserving local refusal of genuinely unknown operations.

4. **[P1] Composition progress does not resume the parked VM.**  
   [Session tick handling](/Users/sto/workspace/datomworld-yin-repl-dht/src/cljc/yin/shell/session.cljc:93) calls `repl/recheck-pending` after serving a response. That operation passes `false` as initial progress; [the driver](/Users/sto/workspace/datomworld-yin-repl-dht/src/cljc/yin/repl.cljc:1460) therefore requires another serving round to make progress before running the VM. Once composition has consumed the request and delivered its response, that additional progress need not occur.

   **Reproduced:** a parked local require received one response through `session/recheck-on-tick` but remained parked. Calling the internal recheck with initial progress `true` completed it as `mod`. The public completion path must explicitly carry readiness into the driver and consume the response once.

5. **[P1] A new publication overwrites an outstanding settlement before consuming its result.**  
   [Publication emission](/Users/sto/workspace/datomworld-yin-repl-dht/src/cljc/yin/repl/index.cljc:478) unconditionally replaces `:pending-publication`. Both `step` and `commit-names` publish before settling queued results.

   **Reproduced:** emit request 1, append its successful result, then commit another transaction. The resulting state has `:published 0`, `:transactions 2`, and pending request 2: request 1’s queued success was discarded as mismatched. If request 2 fails, the engine does not retain request 1’s successful frontier. Consume available results first and explicitly serialize or retain outstanding publications.

6. **[P1] Signed publication answers success before publication completion.**  
   [The extracted `link-answer`](/Users/sto/workspace/datomworld-yin-repl-dht/src/cljc/yin/shell/query.cljc:322) calls `commit-names`, checks only whether `:failure` changed, and immediately constructs an `:ok` response. With externally serviced publication media, `commit-names` can return a pending request with no failure.

   This violates §7’s requirement that signed publication await local publication completion. Retain the call correlation until its envelope commit receives a matching publication result; a later refusal must reach that call.

The reported **102 tests / 1,396 assertions** are useful regression evidence, but they do not establish the new boundary. In particular, [the Step 2 protocol oracle](/Users/sto/workspace/datomworld-yin-repl-dht/test/yin/repl/index_test.cljc:1081) still tests `fixture/accept-result`, not the production result consumer. The [common constructor](/Users/sto/workspace/datomworld-yin-repl-dht/test/yin/repl/fixture.cljc:289) still injects the combined backend handle rather than separately composing content, recovery, policy, and publication service media.

I independently ran the fresh-JVM dependency probe and the three in-memory reproductions above. I did not rerun the reported remote suites or the JVM/Node/Dart matrix. The literal Gate A audit still has nine hits in `store.cljc` and `dht.cljc`; their scheduled relocation is distinct from the active linker dependency defect.

The direct field removals, host-module extraction, generic event shapes, frontier correlation checks, and `notice` correction are sound progress. **Disposition: retain this as intermediate refactor work, not a completed Step 2.** Re-review after fixing the six blockers and moving the protocol/adaptor assertions onto the actual engine/composition path. Full boundary-merge acceptance remains a separate later gate.
